Backend logic first, then the model.

Most of my work starts with an unglamorous question: where does the data actually come from, and what breaks when it's messy? That's how a water-quality dataset of 3,276 samples turned into a full preprocessing and evaluation pipeline, and how a household consumption log turned into a next-day prediction tool people could actually open in a browser.

At Wascrap I work on the Python backend that connects households with scrap collectors — modular workflows, SQL storage, code reviews, and the CI/CD glue that keeps releases boring in a good way.

I care about clean module boundaries, honest metrics, and shipping something a non-technical person can use without a manual.

Aug 2026 — in progress

AI Interviewer

An interview platform that runs a candidate through a structured session end to end. I designed it as separate modules — authentication, candidate workflow, database layer, API surface — and verified each one before wiring them together.

Most of the work was the unfashionable half: authorisation rules, request validation, error paths, and making the frontend and backend agree on the same contract.

Jul 2026

Drinking water quality prediction

An end-to-end pipeline that decides whether a water sample is safe to drink, trained on 3,276 samples across nine physicochemical features. It handles the messy part automatically: missing values, outliers, feature scaling, and exploratory analysis before anything gets trained.

I compared four classification algorithms, then used GridSearchCV to tune the Random Forest — accuracy moved from 65.55% to 67.23%. The final model runs as a Streamlit app anyone can open and test with their own readings.

3,276water samples

Nov 2025

Smart water tank assistant

A decision-support tool that predicts a household's next-day water consumption from its own history, using Decision Tree regression over time-series usage data.

I built the feature-extraction pipeline that turns raw consumption logs into usable signals, then layered on automatic threshold alerts and refill recommendations. The Streamlit interface shows the forecast and the reason behind it, not just a number.

24hforecast horizon
Autothreshold alerts
